executive_summary: The V002 full texts substantially narrow the proposed direction. T1 is closed: NiTi/Nitinol wires already form contacting multiwire ropes or braids whose inter-wire friction, slip constraints, architecture, and phase transformation affect structural response, including bending stiffness and hysteresis. Major non-pressure portions of T3 are also established: prior work directly combines NiTi phase transformation with inter-wire friction/contact, micro-slip, hysteresis, thermomechanical stiffening, and effective structural stiffness or damping. No supplied full text, however, actively varies positive radial/transverse confinement pressure on a NiTi bundle and demonstrates pressure-dependent bending stiffness. Fixed manufacturing pressure, helix-induced contact, axial-load-induced contact, passive preload, and the single fixed radial-pressure submarine-cable simulation do not close T2. The surviving question is therefore limited to actively pressure-controlled NiTi-bundle bending and whether pressure changes transformation-mediated stick-slip mechanics beyond existing elastic-fiber and passive NiTi-cable models. Citation coverage is not closed, so this is not a final survival verdict.

target_audit.target: NiTi/Nitinol wires themselves form a contacting/slipping frictional bundle whose structural stiffness depends on inter-wire interaction.
target_audit.assessment: Direct prior mechanics exist. Mixed and all-NiTi ropes, strands, microcables, and braids exhibit inter-wire contact or slip, frictional hysteresis, architecture-dependent modulus/stiffness, and bending or tensile structural response. Carboni and Lacarbonara directly attribute bending hysteresis to simultaneous inter-wire friction and NiTi transformation; Vahidi et al. model NiTi ropes with Coulomb contact; Liu et al. show braid constraints and micro-slip changing storage modulus; Silva et al. show inter-filament friction changing dynamic stiffening and damping. T1 cannot carry novelty.

target_audit.target: Externally applied positive/confining pressure radially/transversely compresses a metallic/NiTi bundle, changes normal force/friction, and changes structural stiffness.
target_audit.assessment: The matrix contains strong passive-pressure and metallic-cable baselines but no direct actively varied confinement-pressure NiTi-bundle result. Liu's thesis links passive interlayer radial pressure to friction, slip thresholds, and curvature-dependent flexural rigidity. Tjahjanto et al. apply a fixed 0.2 MPa radial pressure in a metallic submarine-cable FE model with frictional cyclic bending. Neither varies confinement pressure as the independent stiffness-control variable, and neither establishes pressure-controlled NiTi-bundle bending stiffness.
missing_mechanics: NiTi bundle subjected to independently and actively varied radial or transverse confinement pressure
Measured pressure-dependent inter-wire normal force or slip threshold
Measured or validated pressure-dependent bending stiffness of the NiTi bundle
Separation of active confinement effects from helix geometry, axial tension, manufacturing preload, and passive internal pressure

target_audit.target: NiTi superelastic/phase-transformation response is coupled with inter-wire contact/slip/friction, confinement pressure, hysteresis and structural stiffness.
target_audit.assessment: NiTi transformation coupled with inter-wire friction/contact, hysteresis, effective stiffness, damping, and thermomechanical response is already established. Direct examples include mixed NiTi-steel ropes in cyclic bending, multiconfiguration Nitinol strand assemblies, frictional 3D SMA-rope models, braided NiTi microfilaments, and dynamically cycled NiTi microcables. Contact regions can initiate transformation, inter-wire friction can add heat and shift transformation stresses, and geometric constraints can change modulus and micro-slip. The unclosed element is actively varied confinement pressure and its effect on NiTi-bundle bending stiffness and transformation-mediated stick-slip.
missing_mechanics: Actively varied confinement pressure coupled to NiTi phase transformation
Pressure-dependent transition among stick, partial slip, and full slip during bending
Direct comparison of pressure-controlled NiTi-bundle data against an elastic-fiber contact model
Validated prediction of pressure-dependent bending hysteresis and tangent stiffness across transformation regimes

paper_threat_assessments.title: Superelastic shape memory alloy cables: Part I – Isothermal tension experiments
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: Full-scale multiwire NiTi cables exhibit architecture-dependent superelastic stiffness, transformation fronts, torque coupling, cyclic hysteresis, and strong static inter-wire constraint under axial loading.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: It does not study bending stick-slip or actively varied radial confinement pressure; lubrication produced little change because axial tests remained dominated by static constraint.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Superelastic Shape Memory Alloy Cables: Part II – Subcomponent Isothermal Responses
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: NiTi cable architecture, contact indentations, helix angle, local bending/twisting, and layer-by-layer phase transformation materially alter cable compliance and reaction torque.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: Its tests are axial and use simplifying no-relative-sliding assumptions; no independent pressure control or pressure-dependent bending stiffness is demonstrated.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Nonlinear Vibration Absorber with Pinched Hysteresis: Theory and Experiments
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: Mixed NiTiNOL-steel wire ropes under cyclic bending exhibit pinched hysteresis and amplitude-dependent effective stiffness from simultaneous inter-wire friction and martensitic transformation.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: The rope is passive and has fixed construction; confinement pressure is neither independently imposed nor varied.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Superelastic NiTi SMA cables: Thermal-mechanical behavior, hysteretic modelling and seismic application
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: A 7x7 NiTi cable has transformation hysteresis, non-synchronous wire engagement, architecture-dependent effective modulus, cyclic degradation, and a reduced multilayer constitutive representation.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: The model does not resolve frictional bending contact or actively controlled confinement pressure.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Nonlinear dynamic response of a wire rope isolator: Experiment, identification and validation
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: For steel wire ropes, inter-wire friction and rope geometry generate amplitude-dependent stiffness, asymmetric hysteresis, and predictable dynamic response.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: It contains no NiTi phase transformation and no active confinement-pressure variable.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Experimental-Numerical Assessment of Mechanical Behavior of Laboratory-Made Steel and NiTi Shape Memory Alloy Wire Ropes
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: A 3D NiTi-rope FE framework combines superelastic constitutive behavior with hard normal contact and penalty friction; wire count and helix angle change transformation response and cable-level stiffness under tension.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: NiTi-rope experiments were not performed, loading was tensile rather than bending, and confinement pressure was not independently controlled.

paper_threat_assessments.title: A new mechanical model of short wire ropes: Theory and experimental validation
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: Established metallic-wire mechanics already provide experimentally validated partial-stick and full-slip bounds for bending stiffness and show that classical perfect-stick beam theory overpredicts stiffness by about an order of magnitude.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: The wires are linearly elastic steel; the model does not resolve contact pressure, progressive wire-by-wire slip, NiTi transformation, or active pressure control.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Finite Element Method for Mechanical Behavior of Shape Memory Alloy Superelastic Cables (形状记忆合金超弹性缆索力学行为的有限单元法)
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: NiTi cable behavior involves coupled material and contact nonlinearities; contact compression localizes stress and initiates transformation at strand interfaces, while a phase-dependent UMAT predicts cable transformation response.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: Friction was deliberately omitted for convergence, the loading was axial, and no externally varied confinement pressure or bending-stiffness test was included.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Hysteresis of Multiconfiguration Assemblies of Nitinol and Steel Strands: Experiments and Phenomenological Identification
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: Nitinol strands under bending, bending-tension, and cyclic loading already exhibit stiffness and pinched hysteresis governed by phase transformation, inter-wire friction, cable stretching, and boundary configuration.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: The varied quantity is assembly kinematics or secondary-member stiffness, not radial confinement pressure or deliberately pressure-modulated friction.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Superelasticity SMA cables and its simplified FE model
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: Reduced FE representations can reproduce axial superelastic hysteresis of multiwire SMA strands and ropes without explicit contact, showing that some cable-level response can be homogenized efficiently.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: The simplified model omits friction and squeezing, is limited to axial tension, and cannot establish pressure-dependent bending or friction-transformation coupling.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Mechanical response of single and double-helix SMA wire ropes
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: A 3D SMA constitutive model combined with normal contact and Coulomb friction predicts superelastic/shape-memory rope response, contact-generated residual stress, friction, transformation, and architecture-dependent force and torque distribution.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: Loading is tensile or thermal-recovery loading, not pressure-controlled bending; normal force originates from rope architecture and loading rather than an actively varied confinement input.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Nonlinear Vibration Isolation via a NiTiNOL Wire Rope
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: A NiTiNOL rope has amplitude-dependent equivalent stiffness and damping under flexural constraints, represented by a beam model plus pinched hysteresis associated with internal friction and phase transition.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: It uses passive rope geometry and secondary experimental data; no confinement-pressure variable is applied.

paper_threat_assessments.title: Cable Vibration Considering Internal Friction
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: The thesis provides valid prior mechanics linking interlayer radial pressure and dry friction to slip thresholds, curvature-dependent flexural rigidity, bending hysteresis, and vibration damping in a multilayer metallic cable.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: Its radial pressure is passive manufacturing/preforming pressure, the cable is linearly elastic rather than NiTi, and pressure is not actively varied as a stiffness-control input.

paper_threat_assessments.title: BENDING MECHANICS OF CABLE CORES AND FILLERS IN A DYNAMIC SUBMARINE CABLE
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: A metallic cable FE model combines externally applied radial pressure, tension, Coulomb contact, relative slip, and cyclic bending mechanics.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: Only one fixed pressure value is applied, the assembly includes polymeric fillers and sheaths rather than a NiTi wire bundle, and pressure-dependent stiffness is not mapped by varying pressure.

paper_threat_assessments.title: High damping capacity with a wide temperature window in braided NiTi microfilaments
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: Braided NiTi directly couples localized martensitic transformation, inter-wire contact micro-slip, geometric constraint, damping, and storage modulus; wire count and braiding density materially alter the response.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: Braiding density is a fixed architectural variable rather than active pressure, tests use small-amplitude axial DMA, and pressure-dependent bending stiffness is not measured.

paper_threat_assessments.title: NiTi SMA Superelastic Micro Cables: Thermomechanical Behavior and Fatigue Life under Dynamic Loadings
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_establishes: Inter-filament friction in a NiTi microcable adds heating and damping; heat accumulation shifts transformation stress through the Clausius-Clapeyron relation and stiffens the cable during dynamic cycling.
paper_threat_assessments.what_it_does_not_establish: Testing is uniaxial tension with no independent radial pressure and no bending-stiffness control experiment.

narrowed_mechanics_core.provisional_surviving_question: Under bending, does independently varied positive radial/transverse confinement pressure change the stick–partial-slip–full-slip transitions, transformation distribution, hysteresis, and tangent stiffness of a NiTi wire bundle in a way not captured by established elastic-wire pressure models or passive NiTi rope models?
narrowed_mechanics_core.assessment: The broad NiTi-bundle mechanics premise no longer survives: NiTi inter-wire friction, transformation-mediated hysteresis, contact-sensitive response, bending behavior, and reduced modeling all have prior art. What survives this matrix is only active confinement pressure as an independent variable in NiTi-bundle bending. That question remains provisional because none of the supplied full texts varies pressure across a NiTi bundle, but citation coverage is not closed.

parameter_substitution_test.assessment: A constant-elastic-modulus/friction substitution is inadequate when loading enters the transformation-active or thermomechanically coupled regime. Supplied evidence shows phase-dependent modulus, transformation plateaus, localized transformation initiated at contact regions, transformation-plus-friction pinched hysteresis, frictional self-heating that shifts transformation stress, and geometry-dependent sequential transformation. These are beyond replacing nylon or steel with one fixed NiTi modulus and friction coefficient. This does not prove that a new pressure-controlled formulation is required in every quasi-static operating range: the surviving work must still demonstrate, through direct model comparison, that an existing elastic-fiber model with calibrated effective parameters fails for the selected pressure, curvature, temperature, and rate domain.

citation_chase_plan.rationale: Citation chasing remains mandatory because no direct full-text kill of the actively pressure-controlled NiTi-bundle core is present and the protocol's backward/forward coverage conditions have not been completed. Backward screening should focus on the direct NiTi friction/transformation lineage and the passive or fixed radial-pressure cable lineage; forward screening should use the preserved core anchor DOIs. The unresolved threat is specifically an earlier or citing source that independently varies radial/transverse pressure on a NiTi or metallic wire bundle and measures bending stiffness, slip transitions, or transformation-coupled hysteresis. Broad keyword searching is not recommended.

recommended_next_action: Proceed with the protocol-bounded citation chase only: screen backward references of the listed high-priority V002 papers and forward citations of the six core anchors, recording database, date, screened count, and unresolved named sources. Kill the direction if this chase finds actively varied pressure-controlled NiTi-bundle bending mechanics, or if a validated existing framework reproduces the proposed response through ordinary effective-parameter substitution. Otherwise retain only the narrow comparative mechanics study—elastic-fiber pressure model versus transformation-aware NiTi contact/slip model—not NiTi material substitution, wire jamming, SMA-plus-jamming, damping, or passive cable hysteresis as novelty.
